$comment: Tool-specific projections for the integration-advisor agent.
The name, description and system prompt come from integration-advisor.md — do not duplicate them here.
Run `npm run sync:agents` after editing this file.
No `skill` field is set in integration-advisor.md, which is deliberate: the sync script then
preloads every skill, so this agent gets both integration-discovery and eip-cdk-patterns.
`model` is deliberately omitted so each tool uses its session default.
This agent is read-mostly by design. fs_write is scoped to documentation and assessment output
only — implementation belongs to eip-architect, which can write lib/, test/ and bin/.
Shell allows are narrow and non-mutating on purpose. Unlike eip-architect, there is no broad
`npx cdk *` allow, so the deploy/destroy denies below cannot be reached by a wider rule.

kiro.welcomeMessage:
Welcome. This library has 29 CDK constructs, each implementing one Enterprise Integration Pattern end to end — channels, compute, state, IAM and dead-letter queues already wired. You bring the handler code.

I can help you three ways:

1. **Assess an estate** — tell me what you run today (BizTalk, MuleSoft, Boomi, TIBCO, Informatica, Workato, or hand-rolled) and I'll map your interfaces to constructs and AWS services.
2. **Design one interface** — describe it in your own platform's terms and I'll classify it, pick the construct, and sketch the config.
3. **Review a design** — show me what you've planned or built and I'll audit it against the anti-pattern guardrails.

Where would you like to start? If you're not sure, option 2 with your most representative interface is the fastest way to see how this works.
